title: They look for the supply route before taking the shot
observation: At 08:08 the crew withholds fire while trying to identify a logistics destination, then moves into woods and discusses mining the main supply artery. The sampled sequence shows the Humvee beside a logistics vehicle and supply crates.
interpretation: This crew treats information, route denial and logistics disruption as useful work away from the infantry fight.
response: Vary logistics routes, scout bridge exits and use a security element. A surviving supply truck may reveal the base even if the crew initially lets it pass.
limitation: Mine kills, total supply denial and a resulting score change are not independently measured.

title: Tyres and repair access constrain the raiding crew
observation: The crew reports a tyre out, exposed positions and a decision to move away around 11 minutes. Later overview frames also show wrench repairs and returns to service areas.
interpretation: The Humvee can disengage quickly, but sustained harassment depends on vehicle health, crew cover and access to repairs.
response: Pressure the vehicle when it has to stop; cover predictable bridge exits and repair approaches rather than chasing it through every back road.
limitation: One crew is observed. The gas-can call is not evidence it actually ran out of fuel.

title: Repeated drill calls have an explicit support loop
observation: At 26:16 the caller assigns someone to watch the drill cooldown and call immediately when available. Further calls request continued fuel; the Humvee offers to carry an extra crate.
interpretation: Red links build readiness, fuel and call timing rather than treating each drill as an isolated action.
response: Watch the supporting fuel and build routes as well as the active objective. Force the next call to compete with repairs or resupply.
limitation: The crew offer is not a verified completed delivery; the builder and full supply inventory are off-camera.

title: Slow demolition keeps useful players off the scoring task
observation: Around 76-79 minutes the crew debates taking versus destroying an enemy FOB, says it needs to be in point and reports the demolition will take much longer. The walled-site sequence continues across several samples.
interpretation: Even during the eventual recovery, task ownership and demolition equipment can make a successful local raid inefficient.
response: If defending, make them spend time clearing a secondary site while protecting the scoring area. In PHNT practice, name a demolition owner and release the rest promptly.
limitation: Time pressure is explicit; the exact points sacrificed to this decision cannot be isolated.

title: They will delay a drill instead of calling automatically
observation: The earlier order is to call on cooldown; at 78:46 the caller changes this to waiting until control is lost. Red later reaches 100.
interpretation: Their objective rhythm adapts to the current favourable zone. Expect a prepared call to remain unused while the existing situation scores.
response: Track both the current scoring area and the reserved call. Do not assume a quiet cooldown means the support chain is broken.
limitation: The final win does not prove the held call was its sole cause.

title: A base-loss call takes a correction to become actionable
observation: Around 49:22 the Humvee crew first treats the destroyed FOB as an enemy loss, then corrects itself: its own FOB has been overrun.
interpretation: Off-screen base status can arrive ambiguously to a roaming crew, delaying a useful task change.
response: Exploit the gap between a base attack and the raiders receiving a clear recall. For PHNT, include owner, location and required response in every base-loss call.
limitation: This is one documented misunderstanding, not a measured team-wide communications failure rate.

title: WARCATS does not convert the large early lead
observation: Blue leads 38-2-1 at 25:00. At 65:00 Red has moved ahead, 51 to 47; the completed result is Blue 56, Red 100, Green 26.
interpretation: A major early lead is recoverable against this recorded side. The samples show a long mid-to-late scoring slowdown, without revealing every reason.
response: Keep a viable scoring and resupply plan when trailing. Look for the transition that lets PHNT re-enter the objective instead of treating the early lead as decisive.
limitation: Direct score evidence; no causal blame is assigned to an unseen WARCATS caller or squad.

title: Green logistics is discoverable from the road network
observation: The Red crew identifies Green logistics moving toward the hot zone and discusses following it, then intercepts along the wooded supply corridor.
interpretation: In this local episode, the delivery approach supplies the opponent with both route information and an interdiction opportunity.
response: Scout before the delivery, vary the last leg and avoid driving a tailing vehicle directly to the FOB.
limitation: The video does not establish how much EASY lost, whether every truck belonged to EASY, or whether this route recurred all match.
